What is leadership?

Great question! Leadership means guiding, directing and influencing other people to work together and achieve a goal. A leader shows the way and helps the group do the right thing. You can see leaders everywhere: the class captain leads the class, the headteacher leads the school, a father or mother leads the family, the village head or Oba leads the community, and the President leads Nigeria. A good leader does not just give orders; a good leader serves the people, sets a good example, and cares for everyone in the group. You too can be a leader!

What are the qualities of a good leader?

Well done for asking! A good leader has these important qualities. Honesty: telling the truth and not cheating. Fairness: treating everyone equally, without favouritism. Hard work: doing their own duties well before asking others to work. Humility: not being proud or bossy. Good listening: hearing other people's ideas and complaints. Courage: standing up for what is right, even when it is difficult. Patience and kindness: correcting others with love, not insults. A class captain who is honest, fair and hardworking earns the respect of classmates. Practise these qualities now, and you will grow into a great leader!

What is followership?

Good question! Followership means supporting, cooperating with and obeying a leader so that the group can reach its goal. Followers are just as important as leaders; a leader with no followers cannot achieve anything! Good followers obey rules and lawful instructions, do their own duties well, support the leader with good ideas, and respectfully speak up when something is wrong. For example, when the class captain asks everyone to keep quiet for the teacher, pupils who cooperate are good followers. Remember, most great leaders started as good followers. Being a good follower is training for leadership!

What are the qualities of a good follower?

Lovely question! A good follower shows these qualities. Obedience: following rules and lawful instructions from leaders like parents, teachers and prefects. Loyalty: supporting the group honestly and not spoiling its name. Cooperation: working peacefully with others to finish tasks. Diligence: doing your own duty well without being forced. Respect: speaking politely to leaders and other members. Honesty: telling the truth, even when it is hard. Courage: politely pointing out when the leader is making a mistake, because good followers are not blind followers. If you practise these in class and at home, you are already building a great character!

Who are some leaders in my school and community?

Great question! Leaders are all around you. In school: the headteacher leads the whole school, teachers lead their classes, the head boy and head girl lead the pupils, prefects lead in their duties, and class captains lead each class. In the community: the traditional ruler, such as the Oba, Emir, Obi or village head, leads the town; religious leaders like pastors and imams guide worshippers; the local government chairman leads the local government area. In the family, parents are the leaders. Each leader has duties and deserves respect. Can you name the leaders in your own school?

Why do we need leaders in the society?

Wonderful question! Leaders are needed for many reasons. They guide the group towards its goals, like a driver steering a bus to its destination. They keep order and peace by making and enforcing rules; without leaders, there would be confusion everywhere. They settle quarrels fairly, like when a teacher settles a disagreement between pupils. They speak for the group and protect its interests, the way the class captain reports the class's needs to the teacher. They also organise people to do big things together, like community leaders organising the clearing of gutters. Good leadership makes life better for everyone!

How can I be a good leader in my class?

I love this question! You can start leading right now. Be a good example: come to school early, keep your uniform neat, do your homework, and speak politely. Be fair: if you are a captain or group leader, treat every classmate equally, whether they are your close friend or not. Help others: explain schoolwork to classmates who find it hard. Be honest: never cover up wrongdoing or lie for anyone. Listen: let others share their ideas during group work. Take responsibility: if you make a mistake, admit it and correct it. Leadership begins with small daily actions. Start today!

What happens when leaders and followers do not cooperate?

Very thoughtful question! When leaders and followers do not cooperate, the whole group suffers. There is confusion and disorder, like a football team where players refuse to listen to the captain; they will surely lose the match. Work does not get done: if pupils ignore the labour prefect, the school compound stays dirty. Quarrels and fighting increase, and the group becomes divided. Progress stops, in the class, the community, and even the country. But when leaders lead well and followers cooperate, the group moves forward like a canoe with everyone paddling in the same direction. Cooperation is the key!
